title: cost-optimization: autosuggest batching/caching defaults and quant profiles + unit-econ CLI
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common customer workloads by shipping safe defaults and an ops-facing unit-econ tool. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: (1) autosuggested batching and KV-caching defaults applied at the route layer, (2) model quantization profile library + selection heuristic for common family/sequence-length combos, (3) a lightweight unit-econ CLI to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs for a given workload and recommend config.

What changed (high level):
- route-level defaults: added heuristic-based batching window and prefix KV cache TTL defaults that are conservative and backoff when latency SLOs are tight.
- quant profiles: introduced curated profiles for fp16/int8/int8-perf variants and model-size-aware fallbacks. Profiles are discovery-only by default; route autosuggest will recommend them but not auto-apply without explicit opt-in.
- unit-econ CLI: new tool under tools/unit-econ that consumes sample traces or synthetic load shapes and outputs expected token cost, latency p50/p95, and recommended batching/cache/quant settings. Exposes --simulate and --apply flags for operators.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add batching/caching defaults and route heuristics
- [x] Add quantization profile library and selection heuristic
- [x] Implement unit-econ CLI with simulate mode and basic apply hook
- [x] Add telemetry for selected recommendations (opt-out)
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + perf canary
- [x] Docs and release notes

Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout over 2 weeks. Week 1: internal opt-in beta. Week 2: enable autosuggest recommendations for managed accounts with email notice. Quant profiles are discovery-only until explicit opt-in. CLI will be shipped in the next minor release and documented in redwood-docs.

Expected impact: typical conversational workloads (avg seq_len 128, bursty traffic) should see 18-32% token-cost reduction in our canary runs with p95 latency within SLO for >95% of requests. We added telemetry keys to monitor regression.

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative about auto-applying quantization; we avoid invisible quality regressions by making quant recommendations explicit and by attaching a quick A/B evaluation hook for SDKs.

Related: ENG-1267 (batching defaults), ENG-1293 (unit economics tooling), SUP-4821 (customer request to suggest cost savings during onboarding).

release_notes: Add autosuggest batching and caching defaults (route-level), a curated quantization profile library (discovery-only), and a unit-econ CLI for estimating cost/latency tradeoffs. Recommendations are opt-in by default for Dedicated/Private. Expected cost reduction for typical workloads: ~20% (varies by model and workload).
notes: Conservative rollout: recommendations only, no automatic model quantization. Telemetry added to detect regressions and trigger rollback. Operators can use tools/unit-econ to verify before applying.
